claims.text: Controlled porosity can be introduced into HfMoTaTiZr through powder bed fusion.
Introducing controlled porosity will reduce the overall density of HfMoTaTiZr.
The solid portions of porous HfMoTaTiZr will retain strength because of the intrinsic properties of the high-entropy alloy.
The solid portions of porous HfMoTaTiZr will retain ductility because of the intrinsic properties of the high-entropy alloy.
Powder-bed-fused porous HfMoTaTiZr will have lower density than as-cast HfMoTaTiZr without a significant loss of mechanical properties.
The predicted retention of mechanical properties applies at room temperature.
The predicted retention of mechanical properties applies at elevated temperatures up to 1000 °C.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of 10.21 g cm−3.
The hypothesis is limited to loading conditions that do not cause significant plastic deformation or fracture.
The amount of porosity that can be introduced without compromising mechanical properties is not known.

contradictions.description: The stated boundary excludes loading that causes significant plastic deformation or fracture, but tensile-strength and ductility testing ordinarily requires plastic deformation and often loading to fracture.
